title: Cosy Systemtest
description:
End-to-end systemtest: a fresh GitHub runner installs Cosy from scratch via install_cosy.sh and drives 20 features through the real UI. Nightly 02:30 UTC.

⚠️ 1 skip is EXPECTED: rcon is quarantined. Every red is a real regression — the v1.0.3 template bug was fixed in v1.1.0 and its exclusions were removed. Details: https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

Channels: release = the installer as published · staging = freshly pushed images.
Each run also emits a trace — open it from the "Runs in window" table.

widgets.title: Release channel — current state
widgets.description: What the published product looks like right now. EXPECTED SKIP: `rcon` is quarantined behind SYSTEMTEST_HEAVY because Minecraft does not boot within budget on a GitHub-hosted runner. Details: https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Passing (release)
widgets.description: Features that passed in the most recent release run. Verified against run 30153115819: 17 of 20 features pass. Counts FEATURES, not series: the outer count wraps a `count by (feature)` so a feature is counted once even if several series carry it. With the data model fixed there is one series per (feature, channel) anyway; the dedup keeps the tile honest while older series are still inside the window, and after any future label change. Caveat during such a window: a feature whose old and new samples disagree is counted in BOTH the passing and the failing tile.

widgets.title: Hours since last release run
widgets.description: Freshness. The nightly runs at 02:30 UTC, so this should stay under 26 h. 999 means no release run has reported for at least 7 days. Alert: CosySystemtestStale.

widgets.title: Feature × time — release
widgets.description: When a feature broke and for how long. Values are carried forward for 26 h, so one nightly sample draws a full day-wide step rather than a dot.

widgets.title: Failing features over time (release)
widgets.description: Stacked band per FAILING feature — the stack height is how many features are red and each band shows exactly when that feature broke and when it recovered. Passing features are filtered out, so the legend only ever names what is actually broken. https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Feature status over time — every feature (release)
widgets.description: 1 = passed, 0 = failed, gap = the feature did not run (skips are deliberately absent from this metric — see 'Features not running' below). Use the legend to isolate a single feature's history.

widgets.title: Features not running over time (release)
widgets.description: A line here means the feature was SKIPPED — untested, which is neither a pass nor a fail. `rcon` is expected. Any other feature appearing here is a coverage regression and is alerted on by CosySystemtestFeatureNotRunning.

widgets.title: Duration trends (release)
widgets.description: Creeping slowness shows up here long before it turns into a timeout.

widgets.title: Feature duration (release)
widgets.description: Wall-clock seconds per feature per run. Skipped features are absent rather than 0, so a quarantined feature cannot masquerade as 'it got fast'.

widgets.title: Suite time (release)
widgets.description: Sum of all feature durations in the last run. The CI job has timeout-minutes: 60; a run that approaches it starts losing features to cancellation.

widgets.title: Slowest feature (release)
widgets.description: Duration of the single slowest feature in the last run.

widgets.title: Features over 120 s (release)
widgets.description: How many features individually took more than two minutes. Watch the trend, not the absolute number — the heavyweight template/Minecraft paths are legitimately slow.

widgets.title: Build under test & drill-down
widgets.description: Which images produced these results, and the GitHub run that recorded them.

widgets.title: Runs in window — release & staging (run time, image tags, report, run & trace)
widgets.description: One row per RUN in the window: when it ran, which image pair it installed, and links to its Playwright report, its GitHub run and its trace. Backed by `cosy_platform_systemtest_run_info` (always 1) — the run-level labels live on THAT metric on purpose. Putting them on the per-feature metrics would give every run its own series, which is what made the count tiles read feature x run and made CosySystemtestFeatureFailing's two-run condition unsatisfiable. Sorted by `cosy.systemtest.run_at` descending: a fixed-width ISO 8601 UTC string sorts lexicographically in exactly chronological order. Excludes channel="pr": PR gate runs are far more frequent than the nightly and would bury it. They have their own table in the PR gate section below.

widgets.title: Staging channel — pre-release builds (heads-up, not an incident)
widgets.description: The staging channel installs a freshly pushed sha-<short> image instead of the published tags, so it answers 'will the NEXT release break this?'. Runs are push-triggered, not nightly, so these tiles look back 7 days and going quiet is normal. Alerting on this channel is notification-only (severity: info).

widgets.title: PR gate — pull requests verified before merge (not the released product)
widgets.description:
Runs of the same suite against images built FROM a pull request, pushed under channel="pr". Every release panel and alert on this dashboard pins channel="release", so nothing here can page anyone or change the released view — a red row means a pull request is broken, not the product.

Deliberately a run table and not pass/fail tiles: the per-feature metrics carry only `feature` and `channel` (convention 11 — run-varying labels on them are what made the count tiles read feature x run), so they CANNOT tell one pull request from another. A `last_over_time` tile would blend unrelated PRs and report whichever finished last. Open a row's trace for its per-feature detail.

No report link: a PR run keeps its Playwright report as a GitHub artifact rather than publishing it to the public bucket, so no hosted URL is derived.

widgets.title: PR gate runs — pull request, image tags, GitHub run & trace
widgets.description: One row per PR gate run. Backed by `cosy_platform_systemtest_run_info`, the only metric carrying run-level labels. `cosy.systemtest.pr_url` is what makes a row placeable — without it a row is a bare GitHub run id. Sorted by `cosy.systemtest.run_at` descending (fixed-width ISO 8601 UTC sorts lexicographically in chronological order).
